headline: Low Water Rations the Reactors
deck: Paks may have to shut within 24–72 hours. Cernavodă Unit 1 is down while Unit 2 remains connected, turning the Danube’s cooling margin into a cross-border replacement-power bill.
body: The Danube has become a power-budget constraint for Hungary and Romania.[E1][E3][E4][E6] At Paks, MVM says the river has fallen through operating thresholds that reduce the margin for cooling-water intake, and a full-station shutdown may be required within 24 to 72 hours if conditions worsen.[E1] The first ration is already visible: Unit 2 was cut to half output from 07:00 on July 30, with the local gauge at minus 121 centimetres.[E2] Hydroinfo’s forecast keeps the direction adverse, taking the Paks level toward roughly minus 131 centimetres by August 4.[E5] The forecast does not settle a shutdown, yet it narrows the planning window for replacement power.[E1][E5]

A low river does not remove all nuclear output at once under the procedures described by Paks.[E1][E2] Operators move through restrictions that preserve cooling margins while reducing generation, and Paks has now advanced from warning to a measurable derating.[E1][E2] The ledger entry is specific: one unit is producing about half of its normal output, while management says the entire station could have to stop on a short clock.[E1][E2] The river writes in centimetres; the grid pays in megawatt-hours.[E1][E2][E5] Each operating step buys cooling margin by surrendering generation before the intake constraint reaches the station as a whole.[E1][E2]

Romania is on a different line of the same account.[E3][E4][E6] Nuclearelectrica placed Cernavoda Unit 1 into a controlled shutdown because Danube flow had fallen enough to constrain operation, describing the action as preventive and safe.[E3] Its July 30 filing corrected the stale claim that both reactors were down: Unit 2 remained connected to the national system, Unit 1 remained safely shut, and Unit 2 could still need to stop if hydrological conditions deteriorated.[E4] The current state is one Romanian reactor offline and one online under a live water constraint.[E4] That distinction matters because Unit 2 is still supplying the grid while water managers and the operator watch the same falling river.[E4][E6]

The documented physical mechanism is narrow.[E1][E6] Paks links falling river stages to limits around cooling-water pumps and the plant’s ability to sustain operation within prescribed conditions.[E1] Romania’s water authority says low Danube flow prompted the Unit 1 stop so Unit 2 could continue operating, while water managers also imposed irrigation restrictions.[E6] These decisions couple power generation and water allocation: the operating rules require output or withdrawals to be trimmed before cooling margins become unsafe.[E1][E6] Preserving Unit 2 therefore consumes part of Romania’s remaining water budget at the same time irrigation users are being restricted.[E6]

For the regional grid, missing output has to be balanced through other domestic generation, imports, reduced demand or some combination; the verified notices do not identify the eventual split.[E1][E2][E3][E4] That is the macro exposure created by the hydrological constraint.[E1][E3][E4] Paks faces the possibility of losing substantially more output on short notice, while Romania is already carrying one reactor outage and trying to preserve the second.[E1][E3][E4] Any imported replacement would transfer part of the constraint into cross-border purchasing, although the notices report no purchase volumes, counterparties or price effects.[E1][E2][E3][E4] The notices establish the size and timing of the physical risk while leaving the financing of replacement supply unresolved.[E1][E2][E3][E4]

Industrial demand is therefore a contingent downstream pressure, rather than a reported curtailment.[E1][E3][E4] No source in the ledger reports compulsory factory shutdowns, directed load shedding or a loss of grid stability.[E1][E3][E4] If Paks moves from a half-unit cut to a station shutdown, or if Cernavoda Unit 2 also disconnects, system operators would have fewer nuclear megawatts and a larger replacement requirement.[E1][E2][E4] Industry could then encounter the shortage through higher market prices, voluntary demand reduction or, under a more severe balance, directed limits; those channels are inference, not current measures.[E1][E2][E4] The industrial question begins with who absorbs that replacement cost before it reaches the harsher question of who switches off.[E1][E2][E4]

The safety null deserves full weight.[E1][E2][E3][E4] Both operators describe controlled or preventive actions within operating rules, and the cited material reports no radiological release, equipment failure or unsafe reactor condition.[E1][E2][E3][E4] A derating or shutdown under low-water procedures shows the constraint being managed even as it removes electricity from the system.[E1][E3] The concrete consequence is allocation: Romania has restricted irrigation while preserving one reactor, Hungary has surrendered half of Unit 2’s output, and further river decline could force both systems to buy, generate or forgo more electricity elsewhere.[E2][E4][E6] The next adverse centimetres would therefore tighten the contest over replacement megawatts and water use.[E1][E4][E5][E6] That distinction remains intact even if both sites ultimately remove more capacity: an orderly shutdown can be economically severe while remaining a safety measure.[E1][E3][E4]

evidence_box.fragment: A full-station shutdown may be needed within 24–72 hours as low river stages constrain cooling-water pump operation.
Unit 2 output was reduced by 50% from 07:00 on July 30 with the Danube at minus 121 centimetres.
Cernavoda Unit 1 entered a controlled shutdown because of low Danube flow; the operator described the action as preventive and safe.
Unit 2 remains connected, Unit 1 remains safely shut, and further hydrological deterioration may require Unit 2 to stop.
The Paks river forecast continues downward toward roughly minus 131 centimetres by August 4.
Low flow led to the Unit 1 stop to preserve Unit 2 operation while irrigation restrictions were imposed.

art.caption: Two nuclear stations draw on the same low river under different operating rules.
